# Support Analytics

`customer_support.support_operations.support_analytics` · v0.1.0 · **draft** · **STUB**

**What is the queue actually telling us, and which of these numbers is lying?**


> Turning ticket data into claims a leader will act on, and refusing to make the ones the data cannot carry. Almost every support metric is trivially gameable — handle time falls when agents rush, deflection rises when help is made harder to find, satisfaction rises when only resolved tickets are surveyed — so the discipline is pairing each headline number with the one that catches its abuse, and never shipping the first without the second. Segmentation beats precision here: an average taken across every queue, plan, channel and product area is usually a very accurate description of nobody.

> Promote by adding outcomes, failure_modes, playbooks, heuristics, mental_models, decision_frameworks, kpis and handoffs, following the queue-management capability in this subdomain. The reason to delay promotion is that this capability describes how to read the other eight subdomains, so authoring it early risks encoding a measurement view of triage, escalation and deflection that those capabilities then contradict. When it is promoted, the load-bearing content is the counter-metric pairing table and the distinction between a metric that measures the work and a metric that measures the people — the two get conflated in every support review deck, and the conflation is what makes teams stop trusting their own dashboards.
